t: A federation of French colonies in West Africa, governed from Saint-Louis and from 1902 from Dakar by a governor-general.
It ruled most Africans as subjects under the indigénat code, with forced labour, head tax and conscription into the tirailleurs.
Post-war reforms shifted power to the territories, and the federation dissolved in 1958–1959 as eight states moved to independence.
dyk: Despite their name, the tirailleurs sénégalais were recruited from across French West Africa, and many came from present-day Mali, Burkina Faso and Guinea rather than Senegal.
ev: A governor-general is created for France’s West African colonies at Saint-Louis
Ernest Roume’s decree gives the federation its own administration and budget in Dakar
Blaise Diagne leads a recruitment drive for the First World War
Vichy forces repel a British and Free French attack on Dakar
French troops fire on tirailleurs at the Thiaroye camp near Dakar
The indigénat and forced labour are abolished and Africans become citizens
The loi-cadre Defferre gives power to elected territorial assemblies
Guinea votes for independence; the federation is wound up

f.founder: French Third Republic (first governor-general Jean-Baptiste Chaudié)
f.predecessor: French Senegal, French Sudan, French Guinea and French Ivory Coast
f.successor: Senegal, Mali, Guinea, Ivory Coast, Burkina Faso, Niger, Benin and Mauritania
